stimulus.title: Testcrosses for pairs of fruit fly genes
stimulus.html:
A researcher studied five genes in fruit flies, labeled V, W, X, Y and Z. For each pair of genes, she crossed females heterozygous for both genes, whose alleles came in known combinations from their parents, with males homozygous recessive for both genes. She then counted the offspring with recombinant (nonparental) combinations.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the recombination frequency for genes W and Z.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Identify the order of genes W, X and Y on the chromosome, and support your answer with data from the table.

rubric.point: Identifies the order W – X – Y (or Y – X – W), supported by W–Y (22.0) being the largest frequency and equal to W–X (9.0) + X–Y (13.0), so X lies between W and Y.
accept: W-X-Y because 9 + 13 = 22, so X is in the middle
X is between W and Y since W-Y is the sum of W-X and X-Y
Y-X-W: the two smaller distances add up to the largest

parts.sample: The order is W – X – Y. W and Y have the largest recombination frequency (22.0%), so they are farthest apart, at the two ends. The other two distances add up to it: W–X (9.0) + X–Y (13.0) = 22.0, which places X between W and Y.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain what the recombination frequency of 49.6% for genes W and V indicates about where V is located.

rubric.point: Explains that about 50% recombination is what independent assortment gives, so V is not linked to W: it is on a different chromosome (or very far from W on the same chromosome).
accept: 49.6% is about 50%, as for unlinked genes, so V is on another chromosome or very far away
W and V assort independently, so they are not linked
near 50% recombinants means the four testcross classes are about equal, as for genes on different chromosomes

parts.sample: A recombination frequency of about 50% means the four testcross classes are about equal, which is what independent assortment produces. So V is not linked to W: it is most likely on a different chromosome, or so far from W on the same chromosome that a crossover between them happens in almost every meiosis.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Gene Z lies between X and Y. Predict the recombination frequency between genes X and Z, and justify your prediction.

rubric.point: Predicts about 5% and justifies from the map: Z is 14 map units from W and X is 9 map units from W, with both on the same side of W, so X–Z ≈ 14 − 9 = 5 map units (and Z–Y ≈ 22 − 14 = 8).
accept: about 5 map units: W-Z 14 minus W-X 9
5% because Z is 14 from W and X is 9 from W, on the same side

parts.sample: About 5%. On the map, X is 9 map units from W and Z is 14 map units from W. Since Z lies between X and Y, both are on the same side of W, so the distance from X to Z is 14 − 9 = 5 map units, which predicts a recombination frequency of about 5% (and about 8% between Z and Y, since 22 − 14 = 8).
